basis: EQT Mid Market bought the majority from the founders (announced 2015-10-05, completed Dec 2015); Project A joined EQT's position with a seven-figure co-investment in March 2016 ('With its seven-figure investment Project A joins the EQT Mid Market Fund', eu-startups), and in April 2023 was part of the management buy-out consortium that bought kfzteile24 from EQT. Control position (decisions.md D3, R1; COLLECTION.md s1 T3).

Bregal Unternehmerkapital completed a majority buyout in early October 2016; Project A put a seven-figure sum into a minority stake beside Bregal in November 2016, its 'second private equity co-investment' (VC Magazin). Control position (decisions.md D3, R1; COLLECTION.md s1 T3).

3i bought the majority of Lampenwelt in March 2017; Project A agreed with 3i to invest in October 2017, 'the third private equity co-investment' (Private Equity News). 3i still holds the majority of LUQOM Group. Control position (decisions.md D3, R1; COLLECTION.md s1 T3).

Bregal Unternehmerkapital bought trendtours from its founder as a succession arrangement in October 2018; Project A Services GmbH & Co. KG joined weeks later as an operational co-investor (VC Magazin, 2018-11-21); the firm's own archived record reads 'Succession Arrangement', 'PE Co-Investment'. Control position (decisions.md D3, R1; COLLECTION.md s1 T3).

3i agreed in September 2020 to buy a majority of A-Z Gartenhaus (renamed YDEON); Project A's October 2020 investment 'was made as a co-investment with the private equity firm 3i Group' (Deutsche Startups dealmonitor). Control position (decisions.md D3, R1; COLLECTION.md s1 T3).

Bregal Unternehmerkapital bought the majority of Perfect Drive Sports Group (All4Golf, Clubhouse Golf) in March 2021; Project A's July 2021 investment was a PE co-investment beside Bregal (YPOG). Control position (decisions.md D3, R1; COLLECTION.md s1 T3).

The same company as the CMS row PDSG, listed 2021-2024 under its full name: Bregal holds the majority and Project A's July 2021 stake was a PE co-investment beside it (YPOG). Control position (decisions.md D3, R1; COLLECTION.md s1 T3).

Oakley Capital bought WindStar Medical from ProSiebenSat.1's NuCom in October 2020, and Project A invested together with Oakley in December 2020 (FYB); the Merz Group took the majority of the combined holding in 2024. Control position (decisions.md D3, R1; COLLECTION.md s1 T3).

Triton completed a majority acquisition of Inwerk on 2020-12-23; Project A invested in the Triton-controlled company in May 2021, recorded by the firm as a 'PE Co-Investment' (the archived Contentful record). Control position (decisions.md D3, R1; COLLECTION.md s1 T3).

Capvis has held the majority since April 2018; Project A's May 2020 investment in the Capvis portfolio company (Capvis's own release) is recorded by the firm as a 'PE Co-Investment', 'Later Stage Acceleration' (the archived Contentful record): a stake beside the controlling sponsor. Control position (decisions.md D3, R1; COLLECTION.md s1 T3).

3i bought the majority from the founder in June-August 2022 (FIH Partners); Project A's 2022 position, from Fund IV, is recorded by the firm as private_equity (live CMS) and 'PE Co-Investment' (archived record), a stake beside 3i. No public source names Project A in the deal. Control position (decisions.md D3, R1; COLLECTION.md s1 T3).

KLAR Partners' funds invested in NWT Group in 2022 with the founders re-investing after selling ('rückbeteiligt', M&A Review); Project A's November 2022 co-investment 'joins KLAR Partners as a growth partner' (YPOG). KLAR's stake is not stated; the firm records the position as private_equity. Control position (decisions.md D3, R1; COLLECTION.md s1 T3).

Held by the firm's 'Buyout Fund I' (live CMS), a buyout-strategy vehicle (strategy desks, T1); Trill Impact took the majority in May 2025. Project A's PE practice describes itself as a partner for 'Management teams looking for an active majority partner' (project-a.pe). Control position (decisions.md D3, R1; COLLECTION.md s1 T3).

HomeToGo SE has been listed in Frankfurt since the September 2021 SPAC merger; Project A's position dates to 2025 (live CMS, private_equity) and Florian Heinemann joined the supervisory board in May 2025. A purchase of shares in a listed company is not a venture entry (T3, public-market purchase; decisions.md D3).

HelloPrint's 2017 minority investment was made 'via their printing holding Onlineprinters' (Bregal Unternehmerkapital): a position of the Bregal-controlled Onlineprinters group, not of a Project A fund (T2, fund money), and inside the control position excluded as onlineprinters.

Listed on the firm's live CMS (Fund IV, 2025, private_equity) and named among the investors in Amboss's EUR 240M round of March 2025 (YPOG, FYB): a minority stake in a company financing with no controlling sponsor (decisions.md D3, R1).

note: Medical knowledge and clinical decision platform, Berlin (founded 2012). Project A came in at the EUR 240M round of March 2025 (KIRKBI, M&G, Lightrock new; part of the money bought out Target Global and Holtzbrinck Digital), a late-stage entry through the PE practice; no company-stated valuation (Bloomberg reported over EUR 800M, below $1B either way).

basis: Listed on the firm's live CMS (Fund IV, 2022, private_equity); Project A co-led Yoummday's EUR 30M growth round of February 2022 with Armira Growth, a minority investor (tech.eu): a company financing with no controlling sponsor (decisions.md D3, R1).

note: Platform for remote customer-service agents, Munich (founded 2015). Project A entered at the EUR 30M growth round of February 2022, co-led with Armira Growth (tech.eu); its counsel calls it a private equity co-investment, but no sponsor holds control.
